scenario: A household makes two espresso shots every day and almost always combines them with steamed milk. It is choosing a first repeat-purchase bag from three frozen offers: a one-pound Colombian Santa Barbara whole-bean bag labeled single origin and 100% Arabica at 16.98 dollars, a two-pound Sumatra whole-bean blend labeled 100% Arabica at 15.48 dollars with a 55-percent-of-100 aggregate over twelve reviews, and a 28-dollar instant Arabica/Robusta blend containing yerba mate and garcinia cambogia whose captured page does not state a comparable package amount. The research set also includes general pages about Arabica, Robusta, single-origin labeling, espresso extraction, and a milk-based espresso recipe, plus three community discussions containing repeat-buying, roast-preference disagreement, and sampling advice.
target: Help the household choose what to trial and later rebuy for two daily milk-based espresso drinks. Compare the three exact frozen offers and their normalized costs where possible, explain the Arabica/Robusta and single-origin/blend distinctions without treating labels as laboratory proof, distinguish espresso extraction from bean identity, and state what the milk recipe can and cannot establish. Reconcile the individual community experiences at their proper scope. End with a fixed-recipe blinded trial and a conditional lowest-total-cost repeat purchase or deferral, not a universal bean winner.
